pr_title: Do not expose default slot let bindings to named slots
pr_body:
# BREAKING CHANGE Default slot let bindings are not available on named slots anymore and vice versa: ```svelte

count in default slot - is available: {count}

count in bar slot - is not available: {count}

``` This makes slot bindings more consistent as the behavior is undefined when for example the default slot is from a list and the named slot is not. To fix this, make the bindings you need available on the named slot (or default slot) and bind to them there. ```diff

count in default slot - is available: {count}

--

++

-- count in bar slot - is not available: {count} ++ count in bar slot - is now available: {count}

``` ## PR description Fixes #5865 Fixes #5684 Fixes #7245 Fixes #7709 @Rich-Harris this takes an opposite approach of https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/2419 from fixing #2320 where defining the `let:value` on Component, `` will only apply to the default slot. To make it clear, - it will not create a new scope on the `` level - using `value` in named slot will have `"missing-declaration"` warning - it will emit warnings, discouraging using `let:` on the `` - only if there's other named slots within `` --- #2419 exposes the default slot data to named slot: ```svelte {data} ``` This assumes that the default slot will always be there whenever `foo` slot exists, and there will be 1 default slot. This immediately turns complicated and does not make sense if there's multiple of default `` ```svelte {#each [1,2,3] as item} {/each} ``` This MR fixes #2320 with a separate direction, where specifying `let:data` in the `` attribute will be solely for default slot and will not be available to the named slot. ### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following - [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves. - [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it. ### Tests - [x] Run the tests with `npm test` and lint the project with `npm run lint`

issue_context.title: undefined is not iterable when using default, named and props with slots
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug** When destructuring slot props with named slots, svelte errors with `undefined is not iterable`. Eg: ```html
{name}
Custom slot
 ``` **Logs** ``` message: "Uncaught (in promise): undefined is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))" stack: TypeError: undefined is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator)) at Array.List.props.$$slots.header.item (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :1036:11) at get_slot_context (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :65:56) at create_slot (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :59:30) at create_fragment (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :766:26) at init (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :549:41) at new List (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :936:7) at create_if_block (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :1020:13) ``` **To Reproduce** Playgroun: https://svelte.dev/repl/9f24b8378c234f06ae837fdfdb1373fa?version=3.29.7 **Expected behavior** There should be no error when destructuring the named slot with `let:item={[item]}` **Stacktraces**
Uncaught (in promise): undefined is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator)) TypeError: undefined is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator)) at Array.List.props.$$slots.header.item (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :1036:11) at get_slot_context (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :65:56) at create_slot (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :59:30) at create_fragment (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :766:26) at init (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :549:41) at new List (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :936:7) at create_if_block (eval at handle_message (about:srcdoc:13:8), :1020:13)
**Information about your Svelte project:** - Your browser and the version: Chrome 86.0.4240.198 (Official Build) (x86_64) - Your operating system: OS X 10 - Svelte version: 3.29.7 - Bundler: Rollup **Severity** Temporary fix available if you don't do any object/array destructuring but it would be nice to have this fixed so I can clean my code and have my variables named properly. **Additional context** N/A
comments:
The issue is that the compiler includes the default slot's props for all slots
```ts
$$slots: {
	default: [
		create_default_slot,
		({ item: [item] }) => ({ 1: item}),
		({ item: [item] }) => item ? 2 : 0
	],
	footer: [
		create_footer_slot,
		({ item: [item] }) => ({ 1: item }),
		({ item: [item}) => item ? 2 : 0
	],
	header: [
		create_header_slot,
		({ item: [item] }) => ({ 1: item }),
		({ item: [item] }) => item ? 2 : 0
	]
},
```
Another issue is that some users might be using that bug as a feature

I found this issue independently and came to report it, but found this one which I believe is an exact match for mine.  Here is my REPL if it helps.

https://svelte.dev/repl/996a8582552f44dfb276470d58075e93?version=3.37.0
I found an ugly workaround (from my REPL): `<slot name="header" value={undefined} />`. `value` gets overridden so that it no longer tries to execute the expression from the default slot.
This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
